title: Adaptive kernel arbitration for heterogeneous quantization pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Design and implement a runtime arbitration layer that selects per-layer execution kernels and numeric paths from a set of calibrated quantization candidates (FP16, FP8, INT8) while enforcing accuracy and latency constraints.

Problem statement:
We have calibration pipelines that produce multiple per-layer quantization candidates for many models (e.g., FP16 baseline, layer-wise FP8, symmetric INT8 for some layers). Currently the runtime has coarse-grained model-level routing to mixed-precision paths which either picks one static profile per model or falls back to FP16. This is suboptimal: some layers tolerate aggressive quantization with large perf/cost wins while others must remain higher precision to preserve output quality.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end token-level p95 latency improves by >= 18% on target Llama-like suites under default batching while maintaining upstream quality regression < 0.5% on curated prompt eval sets.
- Cost-per-token reduction of >= 12% for typical inference workloads (chat and summarization).
- No stability incidents from numerics (no crashes or large divergence) in 2-week canary on dedicated pool.

Design overview:
1) Offline artifacts:
   - Calibration pipeline produces a per-layer candidate list with metadata: numeric type (FP16/FP8/INT8), quantization parameters, calibration trace samples, estimated layerwise error metric (delta log-likelihood or L1 on activations), and kernel compatibility tags (supports-kv-cache, supports-fused-attn, requires-special-kernel). These are stored as compact "quant-candidates" blobs attached to model-version.
   - A lightweight accuracy predictor trained on past calibration runs provides an estimated end-to-end quality delta for a proposed per-layer selection vector.

2) Runtime arbitration components:
   - Cost model: precomputed microbenchmark matrix mapping (kernel, hardware, sequence-length, batch-size) -> p50/p95 latency and memory.
   - Constraint verifier: checks per-request SLO (latency budget), accuracy ceiling (max allowed predicted delta), and hard compatibility (kv-cache, stateful layers).
   - Arbitrate engine: integer linear-programming inspired scorer that balances predicted quality vs latency/cost. Produces a per-model per-layer kernel plan. The engine supports two modes: fast-path greedy (for low overhead) and optimal-solver (used for canaries and batch planning).
   - Plan cache: plans are cached by route+model+typical sequence-length distribution and invalidated when quant-candidates or kernel matrix changes.

3) Safety and fallback:
   - If a selected kernel combination would break kv-cache semantics (e.g., INT8 kernel lacks compatible KV layout), the verifier forces FP16 for those layers or selects a compatible kernel variant.
   - Runtime monitors token-level divergence: if token logprob drift exceeds threshold on a small held-out stream, the request is flagged and rolled back to the safe plan.

Calibration and continuous validation:
- Extend existing calibration job to emit a small validation suite (1000 prompts with gold outputs) and a numeric-sensitivity fingerprint for each model version.
- Implement an A/B evaluation pipeline that runs mixed-precision plans against baseline FP16 on an offline harness and computes: token perplexity delta, exact-match/ROUGE where applicable, and top-k token distribution drift.
- Accept plan if validation metrics are within configured thresholds (default: perplexity delta < 0.5% and max downstream metric regression < 0.5%).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement arbitration engine and plan cache; local microbench validation on 3 small models.
- Phase 2 (canary): deploy to dedicated pool with 5% traffic on non-critical workspaces, enable optimal-solver for canary experiments only.
- Phase 3 (gradual ramp): switch canary to greedy fast-path and enable on host API for low-latency small-batch requests with feature-flag.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Increased scheduling overhead: per-request arbitration must be cheap. We mitigate this with plan caching keyed on coarse request shape and fast-path heuristics.
- Cache footprint: mixed kernels may increase memory fragmentation; enforce per-device mem-safety checks at admission.
- Determinism and reproducibility: stricter regression tests required since mixed-precision can change sampling behaviors; stash seed+plan metadata in traces.
- Observability: add per-request plan tag to tracing, expose plan-level metrics in Console (selected kernels, predicted quality delta, cost delta).

Action items:
- Aisha: finalize quant-candidates schema and land calibration exporter (PR #rwd/quant-export-87).
- Marco: prototype arbitration engine and microbench cost matrix generator.
- Lina Chen: define validation suite and acceptance criteria for the A/B harness.
- Infra: add plan cache eviction metrics and memory-safety knobs to scheduler.

Acceptance_criteria:
- Implementation merged behind feature flag and end-to-end e2e test covering plan selection + fallback paths.
- Canary run for 14 days with no accuracy regression alerts and measured latency + cost gains per success criteria.
- Console dashboard shows per-model plan adoption and per-plan predicted vs observed quality deltas.
acceptance_criteria: Feature-flagged arbitration merges; automated e2e regression tests; 14-day canary with validation suite showing <0.5% quality regression and >12% cost reduction; rollout runbook documented.
